title: DDSVM: A Differentiable Framework for Deep Support Vector Machines with Iterative Geometry-Aware Optimization
claim: Training alternates between building a geometric teacher from frozen features and refining the backbone using that teacher's margin-based targets.
layout: 2 stacked phase panels plus legend, left-to-right flows, red dashed backprop loops
description: A two-row block diagram with a legend strip at the bottom. The top panel, Phase I (Warm-up and Boundary Construction), runs left to right: input image, backbone, last feature layer, then a frozen FC/softmax head feeding a cross-entropy loss. A downward branch extracts frozen features, trains one-vs-rest SVMs, and stores them in a purple hatched 'Boundary Bank'. The bottom panel, Phase II (Geometry-Aware Feature Refinement), passes the input through backbone, L2 normalize and spherical feature h. It then splits into a green Active Feature branch (clean, noise, GAS) and an orange Target branch (distance ranking, squeeze target, detached target). Both feed a red Geometry MSE Loss. Red dashed lines show backprop to the backbone, and a legend explains the colors, flame and snowflake icons, and line styles.
caption: Architectural overview of the proposed DDSVM framework. Phase I (Warm-up and Boundary Construction): the backbone
abstract: Modern deep networks optimize features via cross-entropy without explicit margin maximization, while classical Support Vector Machines maximize the margin on a fixed feature space. Hybrid Deep-SVM approaches typically treat the deep feature extractor as a static input to an SVM head, so SVM geometry never flows back to shape representation learning. We propose the **Differentiable Deep Support Vector Machine (DDSVM)**, an iterative framework that alternates between re-fitting a linear SVM on $L_2$-normalized features and updating the backbone to pull each feature along the SVM-defined margin-widening direction, treating the decision boundary as a dynamic teacher for representation learning. Under spherical normalization the resulting feature gradient lies in the tangent space and optimization focuses exclusively on angular separability. DDSVM reduces top-1 error by **5.6--8.3\%** on image classification benchmarks under data scarcity.
